title: Smooth connected curves: integral, local rings at closed points are DVRs

source.place: Properties Lemma 033M (properties-lemma-normal-Noetherian: a Noetherian normal scheme is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes) for clause 1; Properties Lemma 02IZ (properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring: $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the codimension of $\overline{\{x\}}$) with Algebra Lemma 00PD (algebra-lemma-characterize-dvr) for clause 3; these are the standing hypotheses ('$X$ locally Noetherian integral', local rings DVRs) of Stacks Divisors Lemma 0BE9 specialized to a smooth connected curve

proof.text: *$C$ is Noetherian and regular.* By [def-sc-curves] the structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian ($k$ is a field, so a Noetherian ring, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is one point). Hence $C$ is Noetherian, i.e. locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Since $C$ is smooth over the field $k$, every local ring $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is a regular local ring [lem-sc-smooth-regular]. So $C$ is a locally Noetherian scheme all of whose local rings are regular local rings, i.e. a regular scheme in the second form of [def-weil-regular-scheme], which is the form in which [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] states its hypothesis.

source.place: Properties Lemma 033M (properties-lemma-normal-Noetherian), its hypothesis 'X Noetherian' realized for a scheme of finite type over a field; regularity of the local rings in place of normality, as in the node's source ('smooth over a field gives regular hence normal')

proof.text: *Clause 1: integrality and the function field.* By [def-sc-curves] $C$ is nonempty and connected; by step 1 it is regular. Hence $C$ is integral [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. (This is the route of Properties 033M: a Noetherian normal scheme is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes, and a connected one is integral; [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] states it for regular schemes.) An integral scheme has irreducible underlying space [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible], so the irreducible closed subset $C$ has a unique generic point $\eta$ with $\overline{\{\eta\}}=C$ [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; $\eta$ lies in every nonempty open $V$ (otherwise $\overline{\{\eta\}}\subseteq C\setminus V\neq C$). By [def-sc-function-field] $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$, and it is a field by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] (applied to any nonempty affine open of $C$, which exists since $C$ is a nonempty scheme). For a nonempty open $V$ and $x\in V$, the germ map $\mathcal O_C(V)\to\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and the map of stalks $\rho_x:\mathcal O_{C,x}\to\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ are injective by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] (1) and (2), hence so is their composite, which is $s\mapsto s_\eta$. Moreover $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is a domain with field of fractions $k(C)$ via $\rho_x$ (same node, (2)). This is clause 1.

source.place: Properties Lemma 033M (properties-lemma-normal-Noetherian) for integrality; Morphisms Lemma 01RV and Definition 01RW for $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$

proof.text:
*Distinct points have distinct closures; closed points exist.* If $x,y\in C$ satisfy $\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}$, this irreducible closed subset has the two generic points $x$ and $y$, so $x=y$ by the uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Consequently $C$ is Kolmogorov: for $x
eq y$ the closures differ, so (as $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$ and $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$ together would give equal closures) one of them, say $y$, is not in the closure of the other, and the open set $C\setminus\overline{\{x\}}$ contains $y$ but not $x$. In the same way, if $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$, $x\in\overline{\{z\}}$ and $y
eq x$, $x
eq z$, then $y
eq z$ (else $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, giving $\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}$). $C$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] by step 1. Hence every nonempty closed subset of $C$ contains a closed point of $C$ [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] [def-weil-closed-points]; in particular ($C
eq\emptyset$) $C$ has a closed point.

*Chains of generalizations in $C$ have length at most one, and $C
eq\{\eta\}$.* Suppose $y,x,z\in C$ with $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$, $x\in\overline{\{z\}}$, $y
eq x
eq z$ (so $y
eq z$ by step 3). Then $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{z\}}$ is a chain of length 2 of irreducible closed subsets of $C$ (closures of points are irreducible; the inclusions are strict by step 3), so the topological Krull dimension of $C$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is $\ge2$; and $y=x_0,x,z$ is a chain of generalizations of $y$ of length 2, so $\dim\mathcal O_{C,y}\ge2$ [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] and the dimension of $C$ as the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings [def-pc-dimension] is $\ge2$. Either reading of 'dimension one' in [def-sc-curves] excludes this; so no such $y,x,z$ exist. If $C=\{\eta\}$, its only irreducible closed subset is $C$, so its topological dimension is $0$, and $\dim\mathcal O_{C,\eta}=0$ since $\eta$ has no chain of generalizations of positive length [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains]; both contradict dimension one. So $C$ has a point other than $\eta$, and $\eta$ is not closed (if $\{\eta\}$ were closed, $C=\overline{\{\eta\}}=\{\eta\}$).

*Clause 2.* $\eta$ is not closed and $C$ has a closed point (steps 3, 4). Let $x\in C$, $x
eq\eta$, and suppose $\{x\}$ is not closed. The nonempty closed set $\overline{\{x\}}$ contains a closed point $y$ (step 3), and $y
eq x$ since $\{x\}$ is not closed. Also $x\in C=\overline{\{\eta\}}$ and $x
eq\eta$. So $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$, $x\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$ with $y
eq x
eq\eta$, which step 4 excludes. Hence every point other than $\eta$ is closed.

source.place: Properties Lemma 02IZ (properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring) and Topology Lemma 005E, as combined in steps 3-4

proof.text:
*$\dim\mathcal O_{C,P}=1$ at a closed point $P$.* By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $\dim\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of generalizations of $P$. Since $P$ is closed and $\eta$ is not (step 4), $P
eq\eta$, and $P\in C=\overline{\{\eta\}}$: so $P,\eta$ is a chain of length 1. A chain $P=x_0,x_1,x_2$ of length 2 would give $x_0\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$, $x_1\in\overline{\{x_2\}}$, $x_0
eq x_1
eq x_2$, excluded by step 4. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{C,P}=1$.

*Clause 3: $\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $k(C)$.* $\mathcal O_{C,P}$ is a regular local ring [lem-sc-smooth-regular] of dimension one (step 6), hence a discrete valuation ring [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] (Algebra Lemma 00PD, (3)$\Rightarrow$(1)). By step 2 ([lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] (2)) the injection $\rho_P:\mathcal O_{C,P}\to k(C)$ makes $k(C)$ its field of fractions.

*Clause 3: the normalized valuation.* Write $R=\mathcal O_{C,P}\subseteq k(C)$ (via $\rho_P$) and let $t$ be a uniformizer, $\mathfrak m_R=tR$, $t\neq0$ ($R$ is not a field). $R$ is a Noetherian (principal ideal) local domain with maximal ideal generated by $t$, so every nonzero $b\in R$ is $b=u t^m$ with $u\in R^\times$, $m\ge0$ [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. *Existence:* $f\in k(C)^*$ is $a/b$ with $a,b\in R\setminus\{0\}$ (step 7); writing $a=u_1t^{m_1}$, $b=u_2t^{m_2}$ gives $f=(u_1u_2^{-1})t^{m_1-m_2}$. *Uniqueness:* if $ut^n=u't^{n'}$ with $n>n'$, then $u'=ut^{n-n'}\in tR=\mathfrak m_R$, contradicting $u'\in R^\times$; so $n=n'$ and then $u=u'$. *Independence of $t$:* another uniformizer is $t'=wt$ with $w\in R^\times$ ($t'R=tR$, $R$ a domain), and $ut'^n=(uw^n)t^n$. Hence $v_P(f)=n$ is well defined; $v_P(ff')=v_P(f)+v_P(f')$ by multiplying the two expressions, $v_P(t^n)=n$ gives surjectivity, and $f\in R\setminus\{0\}$ iff $v_P(f)\ge0$ (if $n\ge0$ then $ut^n\in R$; if $f\in R\setminus\{0\}$ the expression $f=ut^m$, $m\ge0$, above is the unique one).

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.smooth_connected_curve_local_rings (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] : ∃ hC : IsIntegral C, letI := hC IsNoetherian C ∧ IsGenericPoint (genericPoint C) (Set.univ : Set C) ∧ IsField C.functionField ∧ (∀ (V : C.Opens) (_ : Nonempty V) (x : V), Function.Injective (C.presheaf.germ V x x.property)) ∧ (∀ x : C, Function.Injective (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk x) C.functionField)) ∧ (∀ x : C, x ≠ genericPoint C → x ∈ closedPoints C) ∧ genericPoint C ∉ closedPoints C ∧ (∃ P : C, P ∈ closedPoints C) ∧ (∀ P : C, P ∈ closedPoints C → IsDiscreteValuationRing (C.presheaf.stalk P) ∧ IsFractionRing (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField ∧ ∃ v : C.functionFieldˣ →* Multiplicative ℤ, Function.Surjective v ∧ (∀ (t : C.presheaf.stalk P), IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk P) = Ideal.span {t} → ∀ g : C.functionFieldˣ, (∃! q : (C.presheaf.stalk P)ˣ × ℤ, (g : C.functionField) = algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField (q.1 : C.presheaf.stalk P) * (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField t) ^ q.2) ∧ (∀ q : (C.presheaf.stalk P)ˣ × ℤ, (g : C.functionField) = algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField (q.1 : C.presheaf.stalk P) * (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField t) ^ q.2 → Multiplicative.toAdd (v g) = q.2)) ∧ (∀ g : C.functionFieldˣ, (∃ r : C.presheaf.stalk P, r ≠ 0 ∧ algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P) C.functionField r = (g : C.functionField)) ↔ 0 ≤ Multiplicative.toAdd (v g)))
